transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I'm here because... I just can't stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot right here around my jaw and my neck. It's just constantly on my mind. And even when folks tell me it looks normal, I just feel like it’s the very first thing the families or the nurses notice when they look at me at work. 

I do personal care, you know, helping out seniors. Actually, just the other day, one of my client's daughters came in—she always wears these really bright, heavy floral scarves, completely out of season if you ask me, but she means well—and we were standing there talking about her mother's meal plan. They keep giving her tapioca pudding at the facility and she absolutely hates tapioca, she always asks for the peach fruit cups. But anyway, while we were talking about the pudding, I just knew she was staring right at my jawline. 

It makes me so uncomfortable. I even feel that way at church, like everybody in the pews is just zeroing in on my neck instead of listening to the pastor. Our pastor just got back from a mission trip, actually, so he's been talking a lot about that... but yeah, I just feel like everyone is looking at this uneven spot on my face.
Has this concern about your jaw and neck area affected your work with the seniors or your interactions with their families in any way?

Well, I guess it has, yeah. I mean, I’ve actually passed up a few chances lately to help lead our staff meetings or take on some of the supervisory pieces. I just get so worked up worrying that if I'm standing up there, everyone will just be staring right at my face and my neck the whole time I'm talking. And those meetings, they always hold them in the main breakroom where the fluorescent lighting is just absolutely awful. It buzzes, too, you know? Like this constant, high-pitched hum that gives you a headache if you sit right under the vent. My coworker Linda actually brought in a little desk lamp with a warm bulb to try and make it better in there, but management made her take it home because of fire codes or something. 

But anyway... yeah, it affects my work. I’ve even fallen behind on my client paperwork lately. I just get stuck in the bathroom at home for so long trying to make myself look presentable before I leave, trying to fix how I look, and before I know it I'm rushing and the paperwork just piles up. 

It’s really spilling over into everything, honestly. I’ve even stopped going to my book club, and my walking club too. Getting ready just feels like way too much effort now. Which is a real shame because the walking club goes right around the big lake at the park, and the ducks are having their babies right now. Little mallards, they're so cute, and people always bring frozen peas to feed them. You're not supposed to feed them bread, you know, it's bad for their stomachs. But yeah, I just... I can't bring myself to get ready and go out to see them anymore.
Do you feel like your concerns about your jaw and neck area are causing you more distress than the actual impact it has on your daily life or relationships?

I mean... I don't know if I'd say it's more distress than the impact, or... I guess I'm not really sure how to weigh the two against each other, you know? It's all just really overwhelming. It just takes up so much room in my head. 

Kind of like how my sister's dog just takes over her whole house. She has this golden retriever, Buster, and he is just massive. I swear he sheds a whole other dog every single week. She bought one of those fancy robot vacuums to try and keep up with the hair, the ones that map out your floor plan? But Buster is terrified of it. He barks at it every time it leaves its little docking station, and then he tries to herd it into the corner like it's a sheep. It's hilarious, honestly, but she can't even run the thing unless she takes him out for a walk first. 

But, um... wait, what were you asking me? About the distress? I just... I don't know if one is worse than the other. It just all feels awful.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions over and over, like checking your appearance, in an attempt to alleviate your concerns about your jaw and neck area?

Oh, constantly. Especially before I leave for work or, you know, if I have a meeting. I just keep going back into the bathroom to check the mirror. We actually just repainted that bathroom, by the way. My husband picked out this color called 'Sea Salt'—it’s supposed to be green, but honestly, in the morning light it looks completely gray. We had to go back to the hardware store three times because he kept underestimating how many gallons we'd need. He always does that, he just absolutely hates asking the people at the paint counter for advice. 

But anyway, yeah, I'll be in there just over and over, fixing my collar, trying to pull my hair down around my neck just right so it hides the unevenness. And then when I finally make it out the door, I'll pull out my phone camera to take another look. The cameras on these new phones are just too much, honestly. My daughter showed me how to use all the settings, but it just captures every single flaw. 

Speaking of my daughter, I end up asking her all the time if it looks strange. I'll say, 'Honey, does my neck look bad today?' and she gets so frustrated with me. She's 19, so she's always a little frustrated, mostly because she's working double shifts at the diner right now trying to save up for a used Honda. They make her wear these awful stiff polyester shirts that don't breathe at all, especially near the fryers... but, um, what was I saying? 

Right, the checking. Between going back to the mirror, checking the phone, and asking my daughter if I look okay... it’s actually made me late for work more than once lately. It's just exhausting.
Do you have any habits or rituals that you feel compelled to do over and over that aren't related to your appearance?

No, I don't think so. I mean, not that I can think of. It's really just the stuff with my face and my neck. I don't have to, like, wash my hands a certain number of times or anything like that. 

Although, my neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she actually does that. She washes her hands so much they get all cracked and bleed in the winter. She uses that really harsh orange soap, you know, the kind mechanics use with the pumice in it? I keep telling her she needs to switch to something gentler, maybe something with shea butter. I found this really wonderful lotion at the farmer's market last weekend—it's lavender and chamomile, made by this lovely couple who keep their own bees. They had all these little jars of local honey, too. I bought one that was infused with jalapeño, if you can believe it. My husband put it on some cornbread the other night and he was sweating through his shirt...

But, no, I don't do anything like that. Just... just the mirror checking and asking my daughter about my neck. That's really it.
Have your concerns about your jaw and neck area changed at all over time, or have they remained the same?

I mean, I don't really think they've changed much. It's just always been this... this constant worry about my jaw and how my neck looks. It feels like it's been the same for as long as I can remember. 

Speaking of things staying the same, the salon where I work hasn't updated its decor since the late nineties. I swear, we still have those awful faux-leather chairs that stick to the back of your legs in the summer. My boss, Linda, she refuses to buy new ones because she says they have "character." But they don't have character, they just have peeling vinyl. She finally let us paint the breakroom, though. We went with this bright sunshine yellow, which sounded nice, but in a room with no windows, it kind of feels like you're sitting inside a lemon. And the smell of the paint mixed with the perm solution we use... oh, it's just a headache waiting to happen. 

But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my neck. No, it hasn't really changed. It's just always there, bothering me exactly the same amount.
Has your concern about your jaw and neck area led to avoiding social interactions or events because you feel self-conscious about your appearance?

Yeah, it... it definitely has. I mean, at work, I've completely passed up chances to help lead staff meetings or, you know, take on any of the supervisory pieces. I just can't stand the thought of standing up there and having everyone staring right at my face and neck while I talk. And I've even fallen behind on my paperwork a few times because I get stuck in the bathroom trying to make myself look presentable before I can even focus on anything else. 

Speaking of paperwork, our new booking system at the salon is an absolute nightmare. They switched us over to this tablet-based app last month, and it crashes every time someone tries to book a balayage. My coworker, Sarah—she just had her second baby, by the way, a little boy, seven pounds, three ounces—she got so mad at the tablet yesterday she almost threw it in the Barbicide jar. I don't blame her, honestly. The old paper appointment book worked just fine. We used to color-code it with these gel pens I bought at the craft store. They had glitter in them! I love a good gel pen. I actually started a bullet journal last year, but I kept messing up the little grids...

Oh, but you were asking about avoiding things. Yeah, it's not just work. I've stopped going to my book club, and I skip my walking club activities a lot now, too. Getting ready just feels like way too much effort, knowing I'm going to look terrible anyway. I just stay home instead.
Is it always specifically your jaw and neck area that you're concerned about, or are there other parts of your body that you worry about as well?

No, it's really just the jaw and the neck. I mean, I don't love my thighs or anything, but who does, right? It's not like the neck thing. That's the only part that really, truly bothers me. 

Although, speaking of thighs, I did try this new Pilates class last week because my sister-in-law swore by it. She said it completely changed her posture. But let me tell you, the instructor was this incredibly intense woman who kept yelling about our "powerhouses." I didn't even know what a powerhouse was! And the mats they had us use were so thin, I felt every single groove in the hardwood floor. They had this beautiful studio, though, right above a bakery. The whole time I was trying to do these leg circles, all I could smell was fresh croissants and cinnamon rolls. It was honestly torture. I went straight downstairs afterward and bought a bear claw. I mean, you have to reward yourself, right? My husband said I shouldn't eat it before dinner, but we were having meatloaf, and I make a terrible meatloaf. I always put too much Worcestershire sauce in it...

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, it's just my neck and my jaw. I don't really fixate on anything else.
Do you think there's a possibility that your jaw and neck area actually looks normal to other people?

I mean, people *say* it looks normal. Folks tell me that all the time. Like, I came in here because I just can't stop seeing this... this sagging, uneven spot right around my jaw and my neck, you know? But everyone swears they don't see it. 

Even at church, they say I look fine. Speaking of church, they just changed the time for the early service last month, which is so frustrating because now I have to completely rush my Sunday mornings. Pastor Dave said it was to accommodate the new children's Sunday school classes, but I honestly think it's just because he wants to get to the golf course earlier before it gets too hot. And the choir robes—they finally washed them after like two years, but whoever did it used some kind of cheap, heavily perfumed detergent, and now half the sopranos are breaking out in hives. It’s a total mess. My friend Brenda, she sings alto, she had to put calamine lotion all over her arms right before the sermon. And she was wearing short sleeves, so everyone could see the pink splotches...

But, um, what were you asking? Oh, if I think it actually looks normal. Yeah, even when folks tell me it looks normal, I just don't believe them. I feel like it’s the absolute first thing families, nurses, or people at church notice when they look at me. It's just glaringly obvious to me, no matter what anybody else says.
Do you think it's possible that the flaw you see in your jaw and neck area isn't actually there, or isn't as noticeable to others as you think it is?

I just... I can't see how that's possible. I mean, I know you just asked me that, and I know what everyone says, but when I look in the mirror, it is right there. It's so obvious. How could they not see it? 

It's like when my husband tried to tell me that the new paint in the living room wasn't too yellow. He kept saying, "It's just a warm cream, honey." But it wasn't! It looked like someone had smeared mustard all over the walls. We had to go back to the hardware store three times to get the right shade. And the guy at the paint counter, his name was Greg, he was so unhelpful. He just kept sighing and looking at his watch like we were the biggest inconvenience in the world. He was wearing this incredibly ugly tie, too—bright purple with little yellow ducks on it. Who wears a duck tie to a hardware store? It made me wonder if he even knew anything about color matching. We finally ended up going with a nice, cool gray, which looks much better with our couch. The couch is navy blue, we got it on sale last Labor Day...

But, no, I just... I don't think it's possible that it's not there. I see it every single day. It's real to me.
Do you think you would feel better about your jaw and neck area if you could be absolutely certain that it looks normal to others?

I don't really know if that would help. I mean, how can you ever be absolutely certain about anything? It's like my client Mrs. Higgins at the salon on Tuesday. She wanted to be absolutely certain that this new gel polish wouldn't chip before her cruise to Alaska. I told her the gel is tough, but I couldn't promise anything if she was going zip-lining or whatever. And she actually is going zip-lining, which is crazy to me because she's got to be at least seventy-five, and she just had her knee replaced last fall. The same doctor did it who fixed my husband's shoulder. Although, my husband still complains about his shoulder every single time it rains. He swears he can feel the barometric pressure dropping in his joints, so he just sits in his recliner and watches the Weather Channel all day. They have that new meteorologist now, the one with the really bad hair extensions. You can literally see the tracks right above her ear when she turns to point at the radar... 

But anyway, what was the question? Oh, feeling better if I knew for a fact it looked normal. I just... I don't know. I can't even imagine what that would feel like, to be honest. I really have no idea.
Have you ever considered seeking a professional opinion, such as a dermatologist or plastic surgeon, to evaluate your jaw and neck area?

Well, um, no, I haven't really thought about going to a plastic surgeon or anything like that. I mean, I guess I could, but doctors are just so expensive these days. It's like when I had to take my cat, Mr. Whiskers, to the vet last month because he wouldn't stop scratching his left ear. Turns out he had ear mites, which I don't even know how he got because he's an indoor cat. But the vet bill was astronomical! And the waiting room smelled like wet dog and industrial cleaner. There was this woman sitting across from me with a Pomeranian in a stroller. A stroller! For a dog! And she had dressed it in a little denim jacket with rhinestones on the back. I just sat there thinking, who has the time or money to buy a bedazzled jacket for a dog that fits in a purse? And she kept feeding it these organic, grain-free treats from a little silver tin...

But, no, to answer your question, I haven't looked into seeing a specialist or a surgeon or anything for my jaw. I just haven't.
Do you think that someone who did not know you and saw you for the first time would notice anything out of the ordinary about your jaw and neck area?

Well, yeah, I do. I came in today because I just can't stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. And honestly, even when folks tell me it looks normal, I feel like it's the very first thing people notice when they look at me. Like, if I meet someone new, say, at church or something. Speaking of church, Pastor Dave had this guest speaker last Sunday, and the man had the most booming voice I've ever heard. It echoed all the way to the back pews, right where I sit next to the stained glass window. The window with the dove on it, you know? Anyway, the speaker was talking about charity, and they passed around the collection plate twice, which I thought was a bit much. I only brought a five-dollar bill, and I had already put it in the first time. The lady next to me, I think her name is Brenda, she gave me this look when I just passed the plate along the second time. She was wearing this hat, too—one of those wide-brimmed things with a fake sunflower stuck to the side. It was so big I had to lean to my left just to see the altar. 

But, yeah, to answer your question, whether it's families I work with, nurses, or just strangers at church... I really do think they see it right away. It's just so obvious to me.
Do you think that if someone took a picture of you from the front, the jaw and neck area would look uneven or abnormal to them?

Well, I don't know about a picture. I guess I'm not really sure if they'd see it in a photo. I try not to let people take pictures of me anyway, especially with smartphones these days. Everyone is always snapping pictures and putting them right on Facebook or Instagram or whatever. My niece, Chloe, she just turned sixteen and she got one of those ring light things for her birthday. She sets it up in the middle of the living room and does these little dances for hours. I don't understand it at all. And she insists on wearing these huge, clunky sneakers with everything, even dresses. I asked my sister why she lets her out of the house looking like that, but my sister just says it's the fashion now. Which reminds me, my sister is trying this new keto diet and all she talks about is cheese and bacon. She came over for dinner last week and practically picked all the toppings off the pizza I ordered. It was from that place down on Main Street, Luigi's? They make a really good crust, kind of thin but not too crispy. 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, a picture. Yeah, I just... I don't know if someone else would think it looks abnormal in a photo. I really couldn't say for sure.
Do you ever find yourself obsessing over other specific details or flaws in your daily life, outside of your appearance?

Well, um, no, not really. I don't think I obsess over other things like that. I mean, I like things to be clean, especially at work. Being a home health aide, you have to keep things sanitary, you know? Like my client, Mr. Henderson, he's such a sweet old man, but he insists on keeping these stacks of old newspapers in his living room. Piles of them, right next to his recliner! I tell him it's a fire hazard, but he says he's going to read them eventually. He's still got papers from 1998 in there. It smells like dust and old coffee in that room. And he drinks his coffee black, just sipping it out of this chipped mug that says "World's Best Grandpa." I offered to buy him a new one at the dollar store—they have those nice ceramic ones with the big handles, you know, easier for arthritis. My aunt had arthritis in her hands, and she used to knit all the time until she couldn't hold the needles anymore. She made me this beautiful afghan once, all purple and yellow squares. It clashed terribly with my sofa, but I kept it folded over the back anyway. 

But, no, I don't really fixate on other flaws or details like that. Just my jaw and neck, really.
Do you think your concerns about your jaw and neck area are the only things that make you feel anxious or self-conscious, or are there other parts of your life where you feel similarly?

Um, no, I don't think so. It's really just my face, you know, the jaw and the neck that gets me all worked up. I don't really get anxious about normal things. Like, driving to my clients' houses, I never get nervous, even when the weather is just awful. We had that terrible ice storm back in February, remember? The roads were just a solid sheet of glass. My little Honda Civic handled it okay, but I saw this massive pickup truck that had slid right into a ditch off Route 9. The guy driving it looked so mad, just standing out there in the freezing rain in a flannel shirt. 

I really don't know why people don't wear proper winter coats anymore. You go to the grocery store and people are wearing shorts in the middle of winter! I was at the Stop & Shop yesterday getting some of those low-sodium soups for Mr. Henderson—he complains they taste like dishwater, but his doctor says he has to watch his blood pressure, so what can you do?—and the boy bagging my groceries was wearing basketball shorts. In thirty-degree weather! I just wanted to tell him he was going to catch his death of cold, but kids don't listen these days. They just stare at their phones. 

But, wait, I'm sorry, what were you asking? Oh, if I get anxious about other parts of my life. No, not really. It's honestly just this sagging around my jaw. That's the only thing that really bothers me.
Do you think it's possible that your perception of your jaw and neck area is not entirely accurate?

Well, I mean, I guess it's possible? But I just... I came in because I can’t stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. It's just right there, you know? And even when folks tell me it looks normal, I just feel like it’s the very first thing families, or the nurses I work with, or people at church notice when they look at me. 

Speaking of church, Pastor Dave gave the longest sermon on Sunday. It was about forgiveness, I think, but he just kept going on and on about this trip he took to the Grand Canyon when he was a boy. He said it took them three days driving in a station wagon with no air conditioning. Can you imagine? I had a station wagon once, a big green Ford Taurus. The AC went out in July, right in the middle of a heatwave. I had to drive to Mrs. Gable's house—she was my client back then, lived way out on County Road 4—and I had all the windows rolled down, sweating right through my scrubs. Mrs. Gable, bless her heart, always kept her house at about eighty degrees anyway because her circulation was so bad. She had these little space heaters in every room, even the bathroom. I was always terrified one of them was going to tip over onto the bath mat. 

But, anyway, what were you saying? Oh, about my jaw being accurate. Yeah, I just... I feel like everyone is staring right at it, even if they say they aren't.
Do you think your concerns about your jaw and neck area are affecting other parts of your life beyond just your appearance?

Well, um, yeah, I suppose it is. I mean, at work, I've actually passed up a few chances to help lead the staff meetings, or take on some of the supervisory pieces. I just... I worry that everyone will just be staring right at my face and neck the whole time I'm talking. And I've even fallen behind on my paperwork a few times because I get stuck in the bathroom mirror, just trying to make myself look presentable before I can even leave the house. 

Leaving the house has gotten harder, actually. I used to go to this book club every Tuesday night at the library. We read mostly mysteries—James Patterson, Mary Higgins Clark, that sort of thing. Mary Higgins Clark was always my favorite. My mother used to read her books all the time. She had a whole bookshelf dedicated just to her in the den. That den always smelled like lavender furniture polish. My mother polished everything every Saturday morning, regular as clockwork. She’d use this yellow rag that had a hole right in the middle of it. I don't know why she never just threw it away and got a new one. 

Anyway, I’ve stopped going to the book club, and I don't go to my walking club on Thursday mornings anymore, either. It just feels like... getting ready, trying to fix my jaw so it doesn't look so awful, it's just too much work. I’d rather just stay home. I used to love walking around the reservoir with the girls. We’d see the ducks, and sometimes those big blue herons. They’re such strange-looking birds, aren’t they? All legs and neck. 

But, um, yes, to answer your question, it definitely affects things. I just can't seem to get past it.
Do you think your jaw and neck area would look different to you if someone you trust told you it looks normal?

I mean, they already do tell me that. My sister, she tells me I look fine all the time. But I don't believe her. I just look in the mirror and I see it, plain as day. It’s right there. 

My sister, though, she’s always been the type to just say whatever makes people happy. She used to do that when we were kids. If my dad made his famous meatloaf—which was always dry as a bone, honestly, he baked it for way too long—she would sit there and tell him it was the best meatloaf she ever had, while feeding half of it to the dog under the table. We had this golden retriever named Buster. He was the sweetest dog, but he had the worst breath. Probably from all that dry meatloaf! He used to chase the mail truck every single day. The mailman, Mr. Peterson, actually started keeping dog biscuits in his pocket just for Buster. Mr. Peterson was such a nice man. He retired a few years ago and moved down to Florida. Naples, I think. Or maybe Fort Myers. Somewhere on the Gulf Coast. I always wanted to visit the Gulf Coast. The water is supposed to be so warm there, not like the ocean here where you freeze your toes off even in August. 

But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right, about trusting people. No, it doesn't really matter who tells me it looks normal. I know what I see, and I just can't unsee it.
